list.title: Systemic symptoms:

list.title: Duration:
list.snippet: Most side effects are short-lived, typically lasting for 1-2 days.

list.title: Rare severe reactions:
list.snippet: Severe allergic reactions are very rare, but if they occur, they can include hives, swelling, difficulty breathing, and rapid heartbeat.

list.title: When to seek medical advice:

text_blocks.snippet: The duration of vaccine symptoms varies depending on the type of vaccine and the individual's immune response. Generally, most vaccine side effects last for 1-3 days. However, some symptoms may persist for longer:

list.snippet: Soreness at the injection site: Can last for up to a week.
Fever, headache, muscle aches: Typically resolve within 2-3 days.
Fatigue: May linger for up to a week or longer.
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea: Usually subside within a few days.

text_blocks.snippet: In rare cases, more serious side effects can occur, such as allergic reactions or seizures. These require immediate medical attention.
It's important to note that the duration of symptoms can also be influenced by factors such as age, overall health, and previous vaccination history.
